I'm tracing a diagonal ray from (8,5) on the 12x12 grid, following it until it hits the left wall at column 0, then reflecting its direction and continuing the path to see where it travels next, reaching the top edge after a few more steps.

I'm working out the remaining three diagonal rays from the source point, tracking each one as it bounces off the grid's edges (right wall, bottom wall) and recording their final resting cells - ending at (2,5), (4,5), (8,1), and (8,11) respectively. Now I'm compiling the full list of cells each ray passes through so I can mark them all with color 8 on the grid.

Now I'm identifying which cells around each endpoint should be marked green, checking the neighboring positions for (2,5), (4,5), (8,1), and (8,11), then beginning to fill in row 0 of the final grid.

Continuing through rows 8 through 11, I'm tracking where each ray value lands versus where the green overwrites take precedence, noting that row9's positions at column 0 and 10 get overwritten to 3 despite the ray originally placing 8 there.

Tracing the diagonal ray from (10,3) with color 7: it travels up-left, hits the wall at column 0, then reflects direction and continues to (4,3), marking each cell along the path.

Following the second ray up-right, it bounces off the right wall at column 9, reflects again off the top wall at row 0, and ends at (2,3), passing through cells like (9,4) through (0,5) then back down to (1,4).

The third and fourth rays go downward, each hitting the bottom wall almost immediately and reflecting to end at (10,1) and (10,5) respectively. Now I'm compiling the full list of cells each ray touches so I can assign the base color 7 to the path and mark the endpoints separately.

I'm marking the four endpoints blue and then placing green diagonal cells around each endpoint. Now I'm filling in the grid row by row, placing 7s along the ray paths, 3s for the green diagonals, and 1s at the endpoints, working through each row's cell values one at a time.

Continuing to fill in the remaining rows of the grid, mapping out the nonzero cell values row by row.
